summary: Does a neder against "vegetables" include gourds? Rabbi Akiva and the Sages argue, using what a messenger sent to buy vegetables would say.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against vegetables
chunks.st: For one who vows that vegetables

chunks.en: may eat gourds.
chunks.st: are forbidden to him, it is permitted for him to eat gourds,

chunks.en: But Rabbi Akiva forbids them.
chunks.st: as people typically do not include gourds in the category of vegetables; and Rabbi Akiva prohibits

chunks.en: They said to Rabbi Akiva,
chunks.st: him from eating gourds. The Rabbis said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: "Doesn't a person tell his messenger, 'Buy
chunks.st: But doesn’t a person say to his agent: Purchase

chunks.en: me vegetables,' and he says, 'I did not
chunks.st: vegetables for me, and

chunks.en: find anything except gourds'?"
chunks.st: the agent, after failing to find vegetables, returns with gourds and says: I found only gourds?

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: This indicates that gourds are not considered vegetables. Rabbi Akiva said to them:

chunks.en: "That is true.
chunks.st: The matter is so,

chunks.en: Or would he tell him,
chunks.st: and that proves my opinion; or perhaps, does the agent return and say:

chunks.en: 'I did not find anything except beans'?
chunks.st: I found only legumes?

chunks.en: Rather, gourds are part of vegetables,
chunks.st: Rather, it is apparent that gourds are included in

chunks.en: but beans are not part of vegetables."
chunks.st: the category of vegetables, although they differ from other vegetables, and therefore, the agent purchases gourds and explains that he found only gourds. And legumes are not included in

chunks.en: And he may not eat fresh Egyptian beans,
chunks.st: the category of vegetables, and that is why the agent dispatched to purchase vegetables would not purchase legumes at all. And for one who vows that vegetables are forbidden to him, it is prohibited to eat the fresh cowpea

chunks.en: but may eat dry ones.
chunks.st: , which is considered a vegetable, and it is permitted to eat dry cowpea, which is not a vegetable.

summary: What does a neder against "dagan" (grain) include? Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against dagan
chunks.st: For one who vows that grain [dagan]

chunks.en: may not eat dry Egyptian beans,
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, it is prohibited to eat the dry cowpea,

chunks.en: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: because, like grain, its final stage of production involves being placed in a pile; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he is only forbidden in the five kinds of grain.
chunks.st: It is prohibited for him to partake of only the five species

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: of grain: Wheat, barley, oats, spelt, and rye, as that is the connotation of the term dagan in the Torah. Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: someone who makes a neder against "tevuah"
chunks.st: For one who vows that grain is forbidden to him, and therefore he will refrain from eating grain [tevua],

chunks.en: is only forbidden in the five kinds.
chunks.st: it is prohibited for him to eat from only the five species

chunks.en: But someone who makes a neder against "dagan"
chunks.st: of grain. However, for one who vows that grain is forbidden to him, and therefore he will refrain from eating grain [dagan],

chunks.en: is forbidden in all of them,
chunks.st: it is prohibited to eat all

chunks.en: but may eat fruit of trees and vegetables.
chunks.st: produce whose final stage of production involves being placed in a pile, e.g., dry cowpea, and it is permitted for him to eat fruits of the tree and vegetables.

summary: A neder against "clothing," "wool," or "linen" is understood by what the person meant. Rabbi Yehudah says it all depends on the person.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against clothing
chunks.st: For one who vows that a garment

chunks.en: may wear sackcloth,
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, it is permitted to wear sackcloth,

chunks.en: a sheet, or a rough cloth.
chunks.st: and to wear a sheet, and to wear a coarse curtain [ḥamila],

chunks.en: If he said, "Konam, wool coming on me,"
chunks.st: as these are not in the category of garments. For one who said: Wool is konam for me and I will therefore not place it upon myself,

chunks.en: he may cover himself with wool fleece.
chunks.st: it is permitted for him to cover himself with wool fleece,
chunks.stMore: which is not considered a garment, and it is prohibited for him to wear only a woolen fabric. For one who said:

chunks.en: "Linen coming on me,"
chunks.st: Flax is konam for me and I will therefore not place it upon myself,

chunks.en: he may cover himself with bundles of flax.
chunks.st: it is permitted for him to cover himself with uncombed flax in bundles,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for him to wear only a flaxen fabric. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: it all depends on the one who made the neder.
chunks.st: Everything is determined according to the one who vows.

chunks.en: If he carried a load, and sweated, and it smelled bad,
chunks.st: If one was bearing a burden of wool and linen, and was sweating, and its smell was unpleasant

chunks.he: אָמַר קוֹנָם צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים עוֹלֶה עָלָי,
chunks.en: and he said, "Konam, wool and linen coming on me,"
chunks.st: for him, and in reaction, he said: Wool and linen are konam for me and I will therefore not place them upon myself,

chunks.en: he may wear them, but may not carry them on his back.
chunks.st: it is permitted
chunks.stMore: for him to cover himself with wool and linen garments, but it is prohibited for him to sling them over his shoulder behind him as a burden. The circumstances of his vow make it clear that he intends to forswear carrying wool and linen as a burden rather than the wearing of them as a garment.

summary: Is the upstairs room part of "the house"? Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against the house
chunks.st: For one who vows that a house

chunks.en: may go into the upstairs room,
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, entry is permitted for him in the upper story

chunks.en: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: of the house; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: the upstairs room is part of the house.
chunks.st: An upper story is included in the house,

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against the upstairs room
chunks.st: and therefore, entry is prohibited there as well. However, for one who vows that an upper story

chunks.en: may go into the house.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, entry is permitted in the house, as the ground floor is not included in the upper story.

summary: Is a "dargash" part of "a bed"? And how far does a neder against a city or a house reach?

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against the bed
chunks.st: For one who vows that a bed

chunks.en: may use a dargash,
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, it is permitted to lie in a dargash,

chunks.en: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: which is not commonly called a bed; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: a dargash is part of "bed."
chunks.st: A dargash is included in the category of a bed.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against the dargash
chunks.st: Everyone agrees that for one who vows that a dargash

chunks.en: may use a bed.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, it is permitted to lie in a bed.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against the city
chunks.st: For one who vows that the city

chunks.en: may go into the city's techum,
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, it is permitted to enter the Shabbat boundary of that city,

words.note: The area around a city where one may walk on Shabbos.

chunks.en: but may not go into the area right next to it.
chunks.st: the two-thousand-cubit area surrounding the city, and it is prohibited to enter its outskirts,

chunks.en: But someone who makes a neder against the house
chunks.st: the seventy-cubit area adjacent to the city. However, for one who vows that a house

chunks.en: is forbidden only from the doorstep and inside.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, it is prohibited to enter only from the doorstop and inward.

summary: If he said "this fruit is konam on me," even what is traded for it or grows from it is forbidden. If he said "that I will not eat," only the fruit itself is forbidden.

chunks.en: "Konam, these fruits are on me,"
chunks.st: For one who says: This produce is konam upon me,

chunks.en: "Konam, they are on my mouth,"
chunks.st: or it is konam upon my mouth,

chunks.en: "Konam, they are to my mouth,"
chunks.st: or it is konam to my mouth,

chunks.en: he may not have what he trades them for, or what grows from them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to partake of the produce, or of its replacements, or of anything that grows from it.

words.en: with what is traded for them
and with what grows from them.

chunks.en: "that I will eat," or "that I will taste,"
chunks.st: If he says: This produce is konam for me, and for that reason I will not eat it, or for that reason I will not taste it,

chunks.en: he may have what he trades them for and what grows from them,
chunks.st: it is permitted for him to partake of its replacements or of anything that grows from it.

words.en: with what is traded for them
and with what grows from them

chunks.en: with a plant whose seed is used up.
chunks.st: This applies only with regard to an item whose seeds cease

chunks.en: But with a plant whose seed is not used up,
chunks.st: after it is sown. However, with regard to an item whose seeds do not cease

chunks.en: even what grows from what grows is forbidden.
chunks.st: after it is sown, e.g., bulbs, which flower and enter into a foliage period and repeat the process, it is prohibited for him to partake even of the growths of its growths, as the original, prohibited item remains intact.

summary: The same rules apply when a man makes a neder against the things his wife makes with her hands.

chunks.en: If a man says to his wife,
chunks.st: For one who says to his wife:

chunks.en: "Konam, the work of your hands is on me,"
chunks.st: Your handicraft is konam upon me,

chunks.en: "Konam, they are on my mouth,"
chunks.st: or it is konam upon my mouth,

chunks.en: "Konam, they are to my mouth,"
chunks.st: or it is konam to my mouth,

chunks.en: he may not have what they are traded for, or what grows from them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to benefit from her handicraft, and from their replacements and anything that grows from them.

words.en: with what is traded for them
and with what grows from them.

chunks.en: "that I will not eat,"
chunks.st: However, if he said to his wife: Your handicraft is konam for me only in the sense that I will not eat

chunks.en: "that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: from your handicraft, or that I will not taste from your handicraft,

chunks.en: he may have what they are traded for, and what grows from them,
chunks.st: it is permitted for him to benefit from their replacements and anything that grows from them.

words.en: with what is traded for them
and with what grows from them

chunks.en: with a plant whose seed is used up.
chunks.st: This applies only with regard to an item whose seeds cease

chunks.en: But with a plant whose seed is not used up,
chunks.st: after it is sown. However, with regard to an item whose seeds do not cease

chunks.en: even what grows from what grows is forbidden.
chunks.st: after it is sown, it is prohibited for him to benefit even from the growths of their growths.

summary: The place of the words "until Pesach" changes the meaning: is it about when he eats, or about when she made it?

chunks.he: שֶׁאַתְּ עוֹשָׂה אֵינִי אוֹכֵל עַד הַפֶּסַח,
chunks.en: "What you make, I will not eat until Pesach,"
chunks.st: If the husband said: From that which you prepare, I will not eat until Passover,

chunks.he: שֶׁאַתְּ עוֹשָׂה אֵינִי מִתְכַּסֶּה עַד הַפֶּסַח,
chunks.en: "What you make, I will not wear until Pesach,"
chunks.st: or, with that which you prepare, I will not cover myself until Passover,

chunks.en: if she made it before Pesach,
chunks.st: then, if she prepared it before Passover,

chunks.en: he may eat it and wear it after Pesach.
chunks.st: it is permitted for him to eat or to cover himself with them after Passover.

chunks.he: שֶׁאַתְּ עוֹשָׂה עַד הַפֶּסַח אֵינִי אוֹכֵל,
chunks.en: "What you make until Pesach, I will not eat,"
chunks.st: If, however, he said: From that which you prepare until Passover, I will not eat,

chunks.he: וְשֶׁאַתְּ עוֹשָׂה עַד הַפֶּסַח אֵינִי מִתְכַּסֶּה,
chunks.en: "and what you make until Pesach, I will not wear,"
chunks.st: or from that which you prepare until Passover, I will not cover myself,

chunks.en: if she made it before Pesach,
chunks.st: then, if she prepared it before Passover,

chunks.en: he may not eat it or wear it after Pesach.
chunks.st: it is prohibited for him to eat or cover himself with it after Passover.

summary: A man made a neder that his wife may not benefit from him if she goes to her father's house. The mishnah explains how the times in his words work.

chunks.he: שֶׁאַתְּ נֶהֱנֵית לִי עַד הַפֶּסַח אִם
chunks.en: "You may not benefit from me until Pesach, if
chunks.st: If he said to her: Benefit from me until Passover if

chunks.en: you go to your father's house until Sukkos,"
chunks.st: you go to your father’s house from now until the festival

chunks.en: if she went before Pesach,
chunks.st: of Sukkot is forbidden for you, and she went to his house before Passover,

chunks.en: she may not benefit from him until Pesach.
chunks.st: it is prohibited for her to derive benefit from him until Passover.

chunks.en: If she went after Pesach,
chunks.explain: And she already got benefit from him before Pesach.
chunks.st: If she derived benefit from him before Passover and went to visit her father after Passover,

chunks.en: she breaks the rule "He shall not break his word."
chunks.st: she is liable for violating the prohibition of: He shall not profane
chunks.stMore: his word (Numbers 30:3), as the condition was fulfilled and she violated the vow retroactively. If the husband vowed:

chunks.he: שֶׁאַתְּ נֶהֱנֵית לִי עַד הֶחָג אִם
chunks.en: "You may not benefit from me until Sukkos, if
chunks.st: Benefit from me is konam for you until the Festival if

chunks.en: you go to your father's house until Pesach,"
chunks.st: you go to your father’s house from now until Passover,

chunks.en: and she went before Pesach,
chunks.st: then if she went to his house before Passover,

chunks.en: she may not benefit from him until Sukkos,
chunks.st: it is prohibited for her to derive benefit from him until the Festival,

chunks.en: and she may go after Pesach.
chunks.st: and it is permitted for her to go to her father’s house after Passover, as that time period is not included in his stipulation.
